analysis:
Documentation-only PR: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (refusal-line table, env passthrough, paths, runtime constants) and docs/provider/sandboxes.md (new `--disk` external-drive section for `darkbloom sandbox setup`). No executable code changed, so no direct security regression is identified.

The documented behavior is relevant to TB-013/T-061 (CLI downloads and runs the add-on installer as the Mac owner) and to A-019. The new `--disk <volume>` flag passes user-supplied paths to the installer. The docs say setup makes paths absolute, checks them with statfs, passes them in order, and never formats a drive. The `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` step is prompted for and not run under `--yes` or without a terminal, which is a reasonable control. The implementation (SandboxAddon/setup path validation, argument passing to install.sh, quoting) is not in the supplied evidence. A later pass should confirm that volume paths cannot inject installer arguments or shell metacharacters, and that setup's sudo invocation is constructed safely.

The external work disk relates to the cache-storage posture in T-041 only by analogy. The sandbox add-on stores VM images and jobs on operator-chosen external media. Its trust assumptions (UUID cloning, retained data on a detached drive, denial of service) are not documented in the threat model. They are outside the provider inference cache, so I record this as a possible threat-model gap rather than a finding.

The cli-reference.md refusal-line table documents fixed, content-free reasons drawn from a closed set. It states that neither the public line nor the private line contains request text, which is consistent with A-001 and does not weaken confidentiality. The env passthrough and App Attest worker-qualification documentation (T-052/T-053) shows no change to authorization semantics; the text says the verified marker never authorizes serving.

Patch excerpts were truncated, so full-diff coverage of cli-reference.md changes at head lines ~1094-1132 and ~1249-1258 was not directly verified; this is a coverage limit.
